candidate.blueprint_topic: Regional analgesia safety teaching and prevention of injury
candidate.educational_objective: Protect an extremity affected by a peripheral nerve block by avoiding unapproved weight-bearing or pressure and maintaining injury precautions until sensation and motor control have adequately returned.

options.A: Do not stand, walk, or put pressure on the affected leg until the care team confirms it is safe; protect the numb limb until sensation and motor control return.
options.B: Bear full weight immediately because absence of pain confirms that the leg can safely support you.
options.C: Apply sustained pressure to the numb area to test whether sensation is returning, even if you cannot feel the pressure.
options.D: Remove prescribed protective devices because nerve-block numbness prevents pressure or fall injuries.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. ASRA Pain Medicine patient guidance explains that regional analgesia can produce temporary numbness, heaviness, weakness, and incomplete muscle control. Patients are instructed to check with the physician or nurse before using an affected extremity for standing or other motor tasks and not to put pressure on an extremity that remains numb. This reduces fall and pressure-injury risk while protective sensation and motor control are impaired. B incorrectly treats pain absence as proof of safe weight-bearing. C can expose an insensate limb to injury. D removes protection precisely when sensory or motor impairment may make injury harder to recognize. The final item uses observable safety actions rather than merely stating that a numb limb should be 'protected.'
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ASRA guidance directly supports temporary sensory/motor impairment after regional blocks, caution with weight-bearing and motor tasks, fall prevention, and avoidance of pressure on a numb extremity.
candidate.source_document_title: Pain Relief After Surgery — Regional Anesthesia Patient Information
candidate.source_locator: ASRA Patient Information → Regional Anesthesia → 'Pain relief after surgery' → Question 4: local anesthetics may cause numbness/heaviness, weight-bearing difficulty and fall risk. Question 6 'What will I feel after the block takes effect?': temporary numbness/heaviness/weakness and reduced muscle control; check with physician/nurse before standing or other motor tasks; do not put pressure on an extremity that feels numb.
